proposals.label: Motta et al. (2019)
proposals.rationale: The only SHOC2 variant in the entry so far is S2G. This paper adds a new SHOC2 mutation, c.807_808delinsTT (p.Gln269_His270delinsHisTyr), in a patient whose hypertrophic cardiomyopathy began before birth. Its functional data point to a mechanism that does not involve membrane targeting: the mutant binds MRAS and PPP1CB more strongly and increases MAPK signaling, but unlike S2G it is not constitutively at the plasma membrane.

paragraphs.text: Motta et al. (2019) reported a RASopathy-causing SHOC2 mutation, c.807_808delinsTT (p.Gln269_His270delinsHisTyr). They described it as the third such SHOC2 mutation and found it in association with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy that began before birth. Structural analyses suggested that the mutation could change how SHOC2's two leucine-rich repeat domains are oriented relative to each other. Compared with wildtype, the mutant protein bound MRAS and PPP1CB more strongly and increased signaling through the MAPK cascade, which supports an activating effect.

paragraphs.text: Jang et al. (2019) characterized a zebrafish shoc2 mutant. proposals.citation: Hannig V, Jeoung M, Jang ER, Phillips JA, Galperin E. A Novel SHOC2 Variant in Rasopathy. Hum Mutat 35: 1290-4, 2014. [PubMed: 25137548]
proposals.label: Hannig et al. (2014)
proposals.rationale: Hannig et al. (2014) report the first SHOC2 variant other than S2G in the entry: M173I (c.519G>A). They describe it as a loss-of-function change that impairs PP1c recruitment. It was inherited from a mildly affected father and caused a milder phenotype, without short stature, heart defects, hyperpigmentation or loose anagen hair. The paper also adds functional data and a genotype-phenotype contrast with S2G.

paragraphs.text: Hannig et al. (2014) described a 5-year-old girl of European ancestry, born to nonconsanguineous parents. She was referred for right optic nerve hypoplasia, bilateral nystagmus, speech delay, poor hair growth, and hyperactive behavior. Her stature was average (47th percentile), and she had macrocephaly (98th percentile), bilateral ptosis, wide-spaced nipples, and clubbed nails. Her hair was sparse and slow-growing but not loose, and her skin pigmentation was normal. MRI showed multiple irregularities of unknown significance in the midbrain, pons, and medulla. Echocardiogram and renal ultrasound were normal. Her father, who carried the same SHOC2 variant, was 6 feet 3 inches tall and had intellectual disability, a high-arched palate, sparse hair, and clubbed nails. His features were very subtle and did not clearly denote a Rasopathy. Both parents had required special education classes.

In childhood and young adulthood she developed hearing loss, strabismus, and hypopituitarism with deficiencies of growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and gonadotropins. The authors noted that true cleft palate did not appear to have been reported before in Noonan syndrome or NSLH. They also noted that endocrine abnormalities other than growth hormone deficiency had rarely been documented. They suggested that the SHOC2 mutation may be responsible for the cleft palate and the hypopituitarism.

paragraphs.text: Zmolikova et al. (2014) reported a girl with molecularly confirmed Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair who had coarctation of the aorta. Prenatal findings were increased nuchal translucency and aortic coarctation with a small ventricular septal defect. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was found after birth. She was born precipitously at 37 weeks and needed resuscitation. She had facial dysmorphism typical of Noonan syndrome, redundant skin over the nape and back, short stature, and relative macrocephaly. She also had failure to thrive with a dystrophic appearance and developmental delay, mainly in motor milestones. Beginning a few weeks after birth, her hair was very thin, sparse, and slow-growing. The authors noted that coarctation of the aorta is not a typical heart defect in this disorder and concluded that their observation extended the phenotypic spectrum.

evidence.statement: Zmolikova et al. (2014) reported a girl with molecularly confirmed NS/LAH who had coarctation of the aorta. Increased nuchal translucency and aortic coarctation with a small ventricular septal defect were noted prenatally, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was detected postnatally. She was born precipitously at 37 weeks and required resuscitation. She had facial dysmorphism typical of Noonan syndrome with redundant skin over the nape and back, short stature, relative macrocephaly, failure to thrive with dystrophic appearance, developmental delay mainly in motor milestones, and very thin, sparse, slow-growing hair beginning a few weeks after birth. The authors noted that coarctation of the aorta is not a typical heart defect in NS/LAH and concluded that their observation extended the phenotypic spectrum.
